finding.claim: _validate_sub accepts tokens with no sub claim even when the caller passes subject=, so a subject-restricted decode is not bound to any subject.
finding.source: Any validly signed token from the same issuer/key that lacks a sub claim (e.g. another token type signed with the same key).
finding.sink: Caller's subject-restricted authorization decision after jwt.decode(..., subject=...).

trace.note: decode_complete passes subject into _validate_claims, which calls _validate_sub when verify_sub is enabled.
_validate_sub returns early when 'sub' is not in the payload.
The subject comparison that would reject a mismatch is never reached for sub-less tokens.
Contrast: _validate_aud raises MissingRequiredClaimError when an expected audience is set and aud is absent.
Contrast: _validate_iss raises MissingRequiredClaimError when an expected issuer is set and iss is absent.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first (api_jws.py:277-285), so the attacker needs a validly signed token. verify_sub defaults to True. No require=['sub'] enforcement by default. Sibling iss/aud checks reject missing claims; sub does not.

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, signing keys are cached per kid with no time-based expiry, so a key removed from the JWKS (revoked) keeps verifying tokens until LRU eviction.
finding.source: Attacker holding the private key of a revoked/removed signing key, presenting tokens with that kid.
finding.sink: get_signing_key_from_jwt returns a cached PyJWK, which is then used to accept the token.

trace.note: lru_cache wraps the bound get_signing_key when cache_keys=True.
get_signing_key is cached by kid; a cache hit returns the old key without consulting the JWKS.
Docstring documents: no time-based expiration; evicted only when cache reaches max size.

finding.guards_checked: cache_keys defaults to False (jwks_client.py:37). Documented trade-off. Requires operator opt-in and attacker possession of the revoked private key. Eviction by requesting other kids is possible.
